title: Minor Chords
description: Play a handful of minor chords and hear how one small change turns bright into moody.

steps.title: One note makes the difference
steps.description: A minor chord is a major chord with its middle note (the third) lowered by one half step. That's the only change, but it shifts the mood from bright to darker and more wistful. C major is C, E, G. C minor is C, Eb, G.

steps.title: C minor
steps.description: Play C, Eb and G. It's the same shape as C major, with your middle finger dropped onto a black key. Hear how much darker it sounds?
steps.hint: Eb is the black key between D and E.

steps.title: A minor
steps.description: A minor is all white keys: A, C, E. It's the same skip-a-key shape you'd use for a major chord.
steps.hint: Thumb on A, middle finger on C, pinky on E.

steps.title: D minor
steps.description: Play D, F and A together. Another minor chord that stays on the white keys.
steps.hint: Start on D, then skip a key twice: D, F, A.

steps.title: E minor
steps.description: Play E, G and B. You'll hear E minor all over pop and rock songs.
steps.hint: Thumb on E, middle finger on G, pinky on B.

steps.title: Back to major
steps.description: Play C major (C, E, G) again and listen to the contrast. After those minor chords, it should sound noticeably brighter.
steps.hint: C, E, G. Your middle finger goes back to the white key E.

steps.title: Spot the difference
steps.description: What actually changes when you go from a major chord to a minor one?

quizOptions.label: The root goes up a half step
